svg.title: Ray time on the head and worker pods
svg.text: Ray on the head and workers: workflow, functions, line numbers and measured times
Code: ej-prj-i4-1 d771518f1, Ray 2.56.1. One sky launch and one sky exec, 6 pods on k8s/kind-skypilot, one echo. Clock times are seconds from the start of sky launch.
The letter beside a time says where it comes from. Time ranges cover the 5 worker pods. The timeline is at the bottom.
trace hook in each Python process (20261104-ray-api-trace)
timestamps in Ray's own logs: gcs_server.out, raylet.out (same run)
Ray's event stats, sky exec window, totals across pods (same run)
import profile on an idle head pod: 5 runs (20261104-driver-imports)
ray start, raylet, per-job Ray workers
Mostly Python start and imports for the ray CLI: GCS itself listened 29
ms after being spawned in a timed run, where this whole box took 1.68 s,
ray start polls every 0.1 s until the dashboard publishes its address
(2.41 s in the timed run), then starts the raylet. This delays the
raylet first log, gRPC server up
dashboard agent, runtime env agent start
Wait for all 6 nodes to be alive
One Python process polling the GCS on the head. The polls are cheap; the
GCS isn't listening until 10.86 s, which explains 3.8 s. The 2.2 s after
that didn't recur: in the timed run, ray start began 30–100 ms after GCS
Imports, then a fixed 2 s sleep in Ray: the worker polls GCS for the
head's node record, in ray/_private/utils.py:1260. Slept twice in the
imports, until the first GCS call
Double the head's 1.01 s. The raylet logs nothing for about 2 s after
starting its agent monitors, then initializes metrics. Cause not
dashboard agent, runtime env agent start
Setup between Ray and the job
18.30 → 21.99 s. SkyPilot, not Ray: rest of the launch, autostop, adding
the job, and queuing it on the head.
Largest fixed cost in the job. import sky runs sky/__init__.py and loads
the whole backend, though the driver uses five modules.
Connect, reserve one bundle per node
GCS asks each raylet to reserve
Counts are from the sky exec job, across all pods.
Waits for new Ray worker processes. 0.956 s in the sky exec job.
Ray worker process starts, runs check_ip
New worker processes for each job. 0.69–0.80 s in the sky exec job. On
the head: 0.41 s here, 0.51 s in the sky exec job.
Submit tasks, wait for each rank
First rank done 3.69 s after driver start. In the sky exec job, all
ranks finished together, 1.36 s after submitting.
Load the task function, run the command
Includes importing what the task function needs. PushTask execution
totals 6.66 s across 10 tasks on workers in the sky exec job.
Nearly all of this is after the last Ray call: Ray's shutdown and
Python's exit. It wasn't broken down further.
Timeline of the sky launch run (seconds from the start of sky launch; worker rows are medians of 5 pods)
Job comparison: the same steps in the launch's job and the sky exec job (seconds)
ray.wait, until the first rank is done
Driver start → first rank done, with small gaps

One sky launch and one sky exec on 6 pods, code ej-prj-i4-1 d771518f1, Ray 2.56.1, kind on one machine, so all pods share a clock. There is no sample size or significance test: use this for structure and
relative size. The driver code is the same for sky jobs launch, but its controller and teardown are not traced here.

The traced image adds the hook to every Python process, and prints Ray stats every 2 s. Never benchmark latency with it. Earlier traces on the plain image gave similar sizes: 3.37 s to GCS and 11.77 s to the
last worker's raylet, on an older image. Import times (M) were measured on the plain bytecode image.

Worker startup: the earlier 7.2 s from GCS to each worker depends on the head. A worker's ray start polls every 2 s until the head's node is registered, which comes after the dashboard wait. In a second, timed
launch (20261104-ray-start-trace), head ray start took 1.68 s to GCS and workers slept twice, 4 s in all. Times differ between the two runs.

Who called whom in RPC rows is inferred from sent and received counts, because Ray's stats do not record the peer of each call. Bands B and C overlap in time, and so do tasks on different nodes. Not shown:
tasks with setup, failures, and cancellation.
